gaps.sentence: ___ , the fire brigade arrived within minutes (LUCKY).
gaps.hint: sentence adverb needed at the start (-ly)
gaps.explanation: A sentence adverb comments on the whole statement: Luckily. The adjective 'lucky' cannot start the sentence.

gaps.sentence: We must ___ our efforts to finish on time (STRONG).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -en forms the verb: strengthen. A base verb follows 'must'.
A bank manager is a person; 'management' is the activity and 'manage' is the verb.

gaps.sentence: She gave a brief ___ of her plans (DESCRIBE).
gaps.explanation: After 'a brief' a noun is needed: description (-tion).

gaps.sentence: His ___ (CONFIDENT) was shaken by the failure.
The success of the launch rests on the ___ (RELY) of the supplier.
gaps.explanation: 'The reliability of the supplier' — the quality noun is needed after 'the'.

gaps.sentence: The thunderstorm was absolutely ___ , so the children hid under the blankets (TERRIFY).
gaps.hint: the storm causes the fear (-ing); note 'terrific' means excellent
gaps.explanation: The storm causes terror, so it is terrifying; the children felt terrified. 'Terrific' means excellent.

gaps.sentence: The street market sells ___ fruit in summer (JUICE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -y forms the adjective: juicy fruit. A comparative or adverb cannot modify 'fruit'.
